title: What can you say about selenium in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 5 wordings for selenium; the strongest is "Helps protect cells from oxidative stress" (strong, 8.25-200 µg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents cancer, or lowers cancer risk, outside FDA's qualified wording".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps protect cells from oxidative stress.
supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 3.5-200 µg a day. EU: at least 8.25 µg, 15% of the 55 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS upper limit: 400 µg.
supported_wordings.form: Selenium from a source on Health Canada's list (such as L-selenomethionine or sodium selenite), counted as selenium

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents cancer, or lowers cancer risk, outside FDA's qualified wording
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names cancer. FDA's qualified claims on selenium and cancer have set wording (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats thyroid disease, such as Hashimoto's or hypothyroidism

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
